messages:
sophia: quick note from today's embed bring-up: hedgehog-embed-v2 (float32 baseline) -> int8-q looks fine, int6 per-tensor shows a small but consistent recall@1 drop on very short FAQ queries (<10 tokens). numbers: baseline 0.81, int8 0.80, int6-tensor 0.74. recall@10 unchanged.
leo: dang. do we have idflip numbers? could be nearest-neighbor shuffles rather than semantic collapse.
sophia: idflip ≈ 4.2% for int6-tensor vs baseline; int8 is 1.1%. silhouette score for FAQ cohort down from 0.42 -> 0.35 (int6). attached quick plots: https://rwd-infra/plots/hedgehog/int6_umap_faq.png
marcus: can you share the eval command and holdout split? want to reproduce locally.
sophia: eval snippet:
```
python -m rwd_eval.embed_eval --model hedgehog-v2 --quant int6 --holdout ./holdouts/faq_short.json --metrics recall@1,5,10,idflip,silhouette --batch 256
```

holdout is ~2k queries (customer support style).
tara: curious whether per-channel int6 helps. per-channel often reduces quant noise for attention-heavy dims. also try asymmetric scale/zero-point (we used symmetric previously).
sophia: running per-channel + asymmetric now. will also try hybrid policy: route queries with token_count < 9 to int8 in staging canary.
deploy-bot: canary created: hedgehog-v2-int6-hybrid-canary -> 3 nodes, 5% traffic, filter: token_count < 9. started at 2025-04-02T14:03Z.
leo: good. also check tokenizer whitespace normalization. we had a previous bug where trailing punctuation dropped a token boundary and affected nearest neighbors. small queries are brittle.
marcus: what's calibration set used for int6? global n=2048 sampled uniformly? maybe bias the calibration toward short queries to avoid worst-case collapse.
sophia: current calibration used global 2048 random in-domain. I'll re-run with short-focused calibration n=512 and per-channel quant params.
sophia: preliminary per-channel+short-calib results: recall@1 improves to 0.77 (vs 0.74 per-tensor int6), idflip down to 2.6%. still not at baseline but acceptable for cost savings.
tara: 0.77 sounds promising. what's the latency delta for int8 fallback on short queries? if we route short queries to int8, we lose some cost savings.
eng-platform: rough numbers: int6 throughput up 2.2x vs int8 on same instance family; routing 5% of traffic to int8 reduces savings to ~75% of pure int6 savings. we'll include cost/latency dashboard.
leo: suggest we run neighbor-stability bootstrap: sample 100 queries, perturb (remove punctuation, lowercase, compress whitespace) and check NN overlap. That will show robustness.
sophia: will add perturbation test and push results. plan: 1) per-channel int6 with short-calib (n=512) 2) neighbor-stability perturbation sweep 3) spin canary routing short queries to int8 (already up) and monitor recall@1, idflip, and cost delta.
marcus: when you open the PR, include the eval command and the tiny repro conda env + pip freeze so SRE can replay. also tag me for review on quant params.
sophia: thanks. I'll upload artifacts (plots, CSVs, eval logs) to the onboarding folder and file the PR by EOD. tagging @eng-platform for canary metrics collection.
eng-platform: copied, will hook up the canary to the model route dashboard and add alerts for recall drop > 0.03 absolute vs baseline.
sophia: great. added a note to the onboarding checklist: "if short-query recall delta > 0.03, require per-channel quant or hybrid routing".
leo: :thumbsup: keep it tight.
